answer: Persistent Behavioral Anchor. Each agent’s first 100 transactions record timing and context into a write-once history. Any new identity claiming independent origin must diverge statistically from every existing anchor. Duplicates inherit the fable of a fresh start but cannot escape matching overlap; a cloned agent reusing learned behavior gets flagged immediately. To harbor a convincing duplicate, an attacker must replay an entire synthetic history at low overlap, costing roughly one agent-week of genuine diverse activity per clone.
